art.title: God the Father
art.why: No NGA Trinity by Masaccio or anyone else; this is the one God as maker, seated on clouds holding a globe, for 'one God, maker of all'. Attribution is 'Circle of'.

art.title: The Baptism of Christ
art.artist: Master of the Saint Bartholomew Altarpiece
art.why: The baptism with the Father above and the scroll 'This is my beloved Son' (the gallery reads the inscription): the baptismal name Father, Son and Spirit. The gallery's description does not mention a dove, so do not claim one.
No NGA painting of a council of bishops or of Nicaea. Codazzi's 'Basilica of Constantine' (4a3f3e1d…) exists but has no gallery description, so it cannot be described; not claimed.
No Hospitality of Abraham (three visitors) in the NGA's open-access paintings; searched titles and descriptions for Abraham, three angels, visitors, Trinity.

art.title: Madonna and Child with God the Father Blessing and Angels
art.why: The gallery describes the Father above, a white dove joined to his hand by rays, and the child below: Father, Spirit and Son in one picture, the nearest NGA has to a Trinity image.

art.title: Salvator Mundi
art.why: No Pantocrator or Transfiguration at NGA. Christ as Saviour of the World, holding and pointing to an open book. The gallery's description does not name the figure (it calls the gender ambiguous); the look text must say only that the title names him.

music.why: Heber's hymn to 'God in three persons, blessed Trinity', sung to the one God of Isaiah's vision.
A prayer to the Holy Spirit, the third name in the baptismal formula; not yet used by any journey.
Orthodox vigil music, the tradition that has said the Nicene Creed unchanged since 381. Also used in Is there a God? s6 (flag).
Spec: none. Optional: ubi-caritas ('where charity and love are, God is there') fits Augustine's lover, beloved and love.
Bach's Credo sets the Nicene Creed; listen for 'Et incarnatus est', the two natures in one person.

memory.title: The Nicene Creed
